headline: I Am The Intern Tasked With Carrying The 'Rejection Cushion' For Athletes Who Refuse Trophies
body:
When I signed up for this internship at the stadium, I expected to handle water bottles or organize team jerseys, not become the official human buffer for award ceremony awkwardness. My job is simple: stand six feet behind the podium with a velvet-covered foam block, ready to intercept any trophy that is politely returned to sender. It’s not just a cushion; it’s a high-density, shock-absorbent masterpiece designed to prevent the precious metal from clattering against the cold stadium tiles.

Yesterday, the atmosphere was incredibly tense, and I could practically feel the silent communication radiating from the podium as the high-ranking official extended the heavy plate. When the team captain politely declined to touch the award, my hands started sweating against the velvet. My manager had explicitly told me, 'If the hardware stays in the air, you move in like a goalkeeper saving a penalty.' I did, and I think I pulled it off with a professional, stony-faced indifference that really obscured the fact that I was shaking.

It’s a peculiar life, standing there in the background of historic sporting moments, waiting for the exact second a celebratory gesture turns into a formal standoff. People don't realize how heavy these trophies are, or how heavy the silence gets when nobody wants to claim them. I’m just an intern trying to get through the post-match ceremony without dropping the award or getting hit by a stray camera boom, yet somehow, I’ve become the most important silent participant in the entire tournament.
